input.body:
Because `copyCursor` uses `permitDefault: true`, the default browser behavior is initiated when there is a selection, causing `useOnCopy` to overwrite the clipboard. This creates a confusing scenario where the `copy` device helper is called but doesn't seem to do anything. This stumped me for a bit while debugging a different issue.

We can't remove `permitDefault: true`, as it is necessary for `useOnCopy` behavior.
We can't remove `ClipboardJS`, as it is necessary for copying the cursor thought when there is no selection.

This needs to be sorted out so there is no overlap, but we need to be careful not to lose existing functionality. Maybe `ClipboardJS` should only be used when there is no browser selection?

Test cases:

- Desktop (keyboard shortcut)
  - Copy collapsed selection
  - Copy uncollapsed selection
  - Copy one multiselected thought
  - Copy many multiselected thoughts
- Mobile (command center)
  - Copy cursor thought in navigation mode
  - Copy multiple thoughts
input.title: copyCursor: `useOnCopy` overwrites ClipboardJS
